Two-Stage Bootstrap Weights for Site/Visit Data

Source: R/nmix.R
nmix_weights.Rd

Draws bootstrap weights for hierarchical data with sites \(i = 1, \ldots, I\) and visits \(j = 1, \ldots, J\). Sites are resampled with replacement, \(u \sim \mathrm{Mult}(I; 1/I, \ldots, 1/I)\); then, within each selected copy of site \(i\), its \(J_i\) observed visits are resampled with replacement, so that the total weight of visit \(j\) is \(W_{ij} \sim \mathrm{Mult}(u_i J_i; 1/J_i, \ldots, 1/J_i)\) and the visit weight is \(v_{ij} = W_{ij} / u_i\). Visits of sites with \(u_i = 0\) or \(J_i = 1\), and missing visits, get \(v_{ij} = 1\).

Usage

nmix_weights(B, obs_mask)

Arguments

B

Positive integer giving the number of bootstrap replicates.

obs_mask

Non-empty logical \(I \times J\) matrix of observed visits without missing values, e.g. loglik$obs_mask from nmix_loglik() or !is.na(y).

Value

A list with site (\(B \times I\)) and visit (\(B \times IJ\), columns ordered as \(i + (j-1)I\)).

Details

Supplying the same weights to several calls of ijk_bootstrap_2stage() gives bootstrap replicates that are coherent across quantities.

Examples

set.seed(1)
w <- nmix_weights(5, matrix(TRUE, 4, 3))
rowSums(w$site)
#> [1] 4 4 4 4 4
